red_flags: Collapse, shoulder-tip pain, or a positive pregnancy test with iliac fossa pain — ruptured ectopic pregnancy; urgent surgical referral
Generalized rigidity and rebound — perforated appendix with peritonitis; urgent surgical referral
Sudden severe pain with vomiting in a woman with a known ovarian cyst — ovarian torsion
Tender irreducible groin lump with the pain — obstructed hernia; urgent surgical referral
High fever with hypotension or confusion — abdominal sepsis
exam: Palpate McBurney's point for tenderness, guarding, and rebound
Test Rovsing's sign — left-sided pressure producing right iliac fossa pain
Perform psoas and obturator maneuvers — pain suggests a retrocecal or pelvic appendix
Palpate for a right iliac fossa mass — appendicular mass, cecal tumor, or Crohn's thickening
Examine both hernial orifices for a lump or cough impulse
Press over the renal angle — tenderness shifts suspicion to urinary causes
Perform a rectal examination — right-sided pelvic tenderness or a mass
Arrange bimanual pelvic assessment where appropriate — adnexal mass or cervical motion tenderness
Examine the throat and cervical lymph nodes — recent viral illness supports mesenteric adenitis

investigations.test: Urine pregnancy test (all women of childbearing age)
investigations.why: Positive makes ectopic pregnancy the leading diagnosis and reframes every other finding; a normal appendix pathway must not start before this result
Leukocytosis supports appendicitis, PID, or diverticulitis; unexplained anemia in an older patient supports cecal carcinoma
Raised values support appendicitis and other inflammatory causes over ureteric colic and functional pain; normal CBC and CRP together make appendicitis less likely
Hematuria supports ureteric stone; marked pyuria supports urinary infection — but mild pyuria can occur with an inflamed appendix lying on the ureter
First-line: non-compressible appendix or appendicular mass, free fluid, adnexal cyst or torsion, tubo-ovarian abscess, and hydronephrosis are each decisive for their differential
Supports pelvic inflammatory disease against appendicitis when discharge and cervical motion tenderness are present
Second-line — if the diagnosis remains unclear, especially over 45: distinguishes appendicitis from cecal diverticulitis, Crohn's ileitis, and a cecal mass
